---
title: "phit-polyfill"
---

phit-polyfill is a pure-PHP implementation of the
[phit](https://github.com/phpstats/phit) extension's functions. When the
extension is not loaded, it defines them in the `Phit` namespace with the
extension's names, parameter names, defaults, result keys, warnings, and
exception codes. Code written against phit runs on hosts where the extension
cannot be installed, such as shared hosting or a managed platform without
custom extensions. When the extension is loaded, the polyfill defines nothing.

The implementations are ports of phit's Rust code. On every input in the test
suites, the polyfill returns the same bits as the extension. It is slower: the
recorded regression fits take 9 to 23 times as long, and mixed models 13 to 78
times as long (see [Compatibility and limitations](php-versions.qmd)).

## Installation

```bash
composer require phpstats/phit-polyfill
```

The polyfill supports PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 (`composer.json` requires
`>=8.3 <8.6`). CI tests all three. No PHP extension is required.

Composer's autoloader loads the polyfill's `bootstrap.php`. If any version
of the `phit` extension is loaded, the bootstrap defines nothing. Otherwise it declares each function the
polyfill implements, unless a function of that name already exists.

The polyfill's functions throw an exception with code 1007 while OPcache's JIT
compiles the process. Set `opcache.jit=disable` where the polyfill runs.

## Usage

Import functions with `use function`, or call them by their qualified names.

```php
use function Phit\fit_ols;

$fit = fit_ols(
    x: [[1.2, 0.4], [2.3, 1.1], [3.1, 0.9], [4.8, 2.2], [5.0, 1.7]],
    y: [2.1, 4.2, 5.8, 8.1, 10.2],
);

$fit['coefficients'];
$fit['p_values'];
```

`$fit['coefficients']` is `[-0.2843, 2.5864, -1.6819]` (rounded here), with
the intercept first. The same code runs with the extension loaded.

## Checking what is available

`Phit\Polyfill\Polyfill` reports which functions the polyfill implements and
whether the extension is loaded.

```php
use Phit\Polyfill\Polyfill;

Polyfill::supports('Phit\fit_logistic');  // true
Polyfill::supports('Phit\read_csv');      // false: needs the extension
Polyfill::nativeLoaded();                 // whether phit is loaded
```

`Polyfill::implementation('Phit\fit_ols')` returns the polyfill's callable
even when the extension is loaded, and it skips the JIT check. The parity
tests and the benchmarks use it to run both implementations in one process.

## Versions

Each polyfill release reproduces one phit release, whose commit is pinned in
`tests/fixtures/REFERENCE`.

| Polyfill | phit |
|---|---|
| 0.3.0 | v0.3.0 (`2629fe1`) |
| 0.2.0 | v0.2.0 (`ac176ff`) |
| 0.1.0 | v0.1.1 (`f4887a4`) |
